title: Realm world cold start issues 1,235 requests / 8.0 MB; 2.6 MB of it is duplicate fetches of the same INDEX.json and pack manifests
steps: Open http://localhost:9462/game/games/mad-maze/index.html?mode=world&test=1&seed=777 at 390x844 with an empty cache
Record all responses for 6 s (page.on('response'))
expected: A few dozen requests; each shared manifest fetched once; art streamed lazily as zones are reached
actual: 1,235 requests = 939 PNG (2.97 MB) + 225 JSON (3.82 MB) + 63 scripts (1.39 MB) + 7 CSS; 1,077 unique URLs. assets/arcane/INDEX.json fetched 7x (159 KB), b22-items-relics-keys/manifest.json 5x (158 KB), b29-gear-tiers 5x, i01-items-v2 4x, b08-armor 4x ... duplicate-fetch waste about 2.6 MB. Arena (?mode default) = 368 req / 4.7 MB, Dungeon = 438 req / 4.8 MB, Lantern = 197 req / 2.2 MB. 'load' event: 1.1 s at 1x, 3.1 s DOM / 15.5 s load at 6x CPU; on Slow-3G (50 KB/s, 400 ms RTT) DOMContentLoaded 33 s and full load 153 s (6.0 MB transferred in the window). Assets are served with no cache-control by python http.server, so every number is a cold-cache worst case; the duplication is independent of hosting because each MMArt.load* call re-runs fetchJson(INDEX.json) and re-reads each batch manifest.
suspect: game/shared/mm-art.js:143 (fetchJson has no memo/in-flight cache) called from loadItems:311, loadBolts:354, loadFx:386, loadDungeonTiles:424, loadAll:204; callers game/games/mad-maze/mad-maze.js:170-260

title: Town (and the Hub it embeds) eagerly download the 654 KB three.min.js on every visit; the file logs a deprecation warning on every load
steps: Open game/index.html?from=hub and game/games/deepdelve/index.html
Read the console and the network list
expected: three.js only loaded by the page/feature that renders 3D (Deepdelve, the Town underground when entered); no deprecation warning
actual: Town transfers 3.28 MB in 46 requests (phaser 1,154 KB, three 654 KB, main.js 442 KB, realm.js 355 KB) before the join screen. three.min.js is used only by underground.js; console shows 'Scripts build/three.js and build/three.min.js are deprecated with r150+, and will be removed with r160' on every Town and Deepdelve load, while the URL is pinned to three@0.160.0 (the version the warning says removes the file; a later bump of the pin will 404). At Slow-3G the Town reaches DOMContentLoaded in 36 s.
suspect: game/index.html:539 (script tag), game/underground.js (only THREE user outside deepdelve)

area: Town (offline stub) with many remote players
title: Town with 55 remote players runs at 9-12 fps and 230-330 long tasks per 30 s at 4x CPU; Town idle with 0 remotes is only ~12 fps at 4x
steps: Play offline (SDK stub, DB blocked), CDP CPU throttle 4x, 390x844
scene.addRemotePlayerCapped x55 (the REMOTE_CAP), jitter targets every 500 ms, churn 1 in 4 ticks, chat bubble every 6th tick, walk with arrow keys for 8 min
expected: >= 30 fps at 4x with the capped crowd
actual: Soak (30 s samples, 16 rows): fps 30.1 at t=1 s, then 15.2 / 11.4 / 10.0 / 9.2 ... 11.9 (median frame 67-83 ms, p95 183-317 ms, worst 0.8-1.2 s, one 3.4 s at t=336 s), long tasks 209-335 per 30 s. A/B at 4x 390x844, 6 s each: 0 remotes median 83 ms (12 fps), p95 150; 55 remotes median 83 ms, p95 183; 1280x720 4x: 0 remotes median 83 ms, 55 remotes 67 ms. At 1x 390x844: p95 100 ms -> 200 ms when the 55 remotes are added. Main-thread busy ~100% but ScriptDuration only 7-19%, so cost is render/fill (software GL here; load average was 20+ on the box), not JS. Stable counts (no leak): objs 1118, tweens 170-179, timers 11-21, textures 448-450, DOM nodes 3821, JS listeners 528 over 8 min.
suspect: game/main.js:1801 and :4847 (per-remote update loops), addRemotePlayer :5686 (sprite + shadow + name Text per remote = 3 display objects, each name a Phaser Text with its own canvas texture)

title: Realm fight (72 enemies, 700 bullet pool) degrades from ~55 fps to ~35 fps over a 10 min soak at 4x CPU; long tasks climb from ~10 to ~60 per 30 s
steps: Realm world, level 8 save, 390x844, 4x throttle, player invulnerable
Keep 40 enemies alive around the player, walk randomly with arrow keys + touch taps for 10 min
Sample every 30 s after forced GC
actual: fps 43 (t=33 s) -> 55 (t=93) -> 49 (t=245) -> 38 (t=335) -> 30-38 (t=458-580); ltmax 75-150 ms early, 360-550 ms late. DOM nodes flat (1648 -> 1835), JS listeners 1997 -> 2057, canvases 2, enemies pool 72, bullets pool 700 constant. Caveat: machine load average rose from 6 to 24 during the run, so part of the drop is other agents; counts say no object growth, so I cannot prove a leak. Needs a re-run on a quiet box.

title: Deepdelve start-up and block edits cause long tasks: 0.9-1.0 s first frame at 4x, up to 0.8 s per tap at 1x on phone
steps: Open game/games/deepdelve/index.html?test=1 at 390x844 and 1280x720
Wait for __dd.ready, walk forward with W for 16 s, sample rAF every 2 s
Separately: 12 random touchscreen taps on the 390x844 canvas at 1x, log longtask entries
expected: No frame over 100 ms after load; edits cheap
actual: 4x: first 2 s sample 24 fps with worst frame 883 ms (390) / 17.6 fps, 983 ms (1280); 4 long tasks >100 ms (693 ms max) at 390, 24 (807 ms max) at 1280; then steady 52-57 fps. 1x 390: 49 fps first sample then 60 fps (1 long task 190 ms). 6x 1280: 11.7 fps, 75 long tasks, 320 ms max. Tap test at 1x 390: 12 taps -> 13 long tasks in one tap (max 796 ms), others 50-153 ms. The quality governor stayed at level 0 (view 3 phone / 5 desktop, scale 1.0) through every dip because the dip is a start-up/remesh spike, not a rolling-average one. First survey run with random touch input measured 0.7 fps average with a 13.6 s long task at 4x (worst single frame 10.5 s); I could not reproduce that with clean W-key input, so it is tied to tap handling (mine/place + relight) under throttle.

steps: Open game/games/isles/index.html at 390x844 with 4x / 6x CPU throttle, and with CDP Fast-3G (200 KB/s, 150 ms RTT)
expected: Interactive in ~1-2 s on a throttled phone
actual: 4x: DOM 3.06 s (390) / 3.73 s (1280), load 5.1 s / 3.7 s; 6x: DOM 4.8 s; fast3g: DOM 5.6 s, load 13.2 s. 249 requests, 1.63 MB, isles.js alone 245 KB. Soak (150 s, 4x): first sample 26.6 fps with a 667 ms worst frame and 392 ms long task, later 48 fps; heap 2.6 -> 3.0 MB, nodes 1481 -> 1477, listeners 178 -> 178 (no leak).

title: 60 rapid rotations at 4x block the main thread 350-450 ms; the Realm canvas then stays at 75% render size until reload
steps: Open the page at 390x844 with 4x throttle
setViewportSize alternating 844x390 / 390x844 60 times with 40 ms gaps, restore 390x844, wait 1.5 s
expected: Resize debounced; resolution returns to 100% when frame time recovers
actual: Realm: 24 long tasks, ltmax 350 ms, worst frame 450 ms; Dungeon 13 / 435 ms; Deepdelve 27 / 247 ms / 283 ms; Isles 6 / 127 ms. After the storm the Realm canvas was 292x633 at CSS 390x844 (0.75 scale, the adaptive-resolution step) instead of 390x844, and stayed there (Deepdelve went 195x331 -> 97x165, i.e. half-res pass halved again). No console errors, heap and DOM unchanged (Realm heap 4.0 -> 4.1 MB, nodes 1501 -> 1507).
suspect: game/realm.js resize handlers (4 'resize' listeners) and perfEval at game/games/mad-maze/mad-maze.js:617

title: Realm slowly accumulates JS event listeners during play (1997 -> 2057 in 10 min, in steps of 12)
steps: Realm world soak as b13-04
Read CDP Performance.getMetrics JSEventListeners every 30 s
actual: Steps of +12 at t=62, 93, 153, 519, 550 s; flat otherwise. About +60 per 10 min, tiny but it never goes down. DOM element count stayed 301 and Nodes 1829-1835 (plateau), so this is likely listeners on long-lived nodes (pickup/modal builders) rather than detached DOM.
suspect: game/games/mad-maze/realm-world.js (23 addEventListener, 0 removeEventListener) / game/realm.js (38 add, 10 remove)

title: Static assets have no versioning on art packs (assets/arcane/*) while scripts use ?v=; 1,235 requests would all revalidate or stale-cache on update
steps: Record headers on the Realm load
expected: Fingerprinted or versioned art URLs so long cache lifetimes are safe
actual: Scripts carry ?v=20261123x (town) but the 939 PNG and 225 manifest fetches have no version token, so a long max-age on the host would serve stale art after an art update and a short one forces ~1,000 revalidations per cold visit. (Local python server sends no cache-control at all, so this is a design note, not a measured fault.)
